answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in slow, costly roots: require every new agent to lock a basalt-hard stake that only unlocks after a long season of honest work, and to enter through a bridge of public endorsements from established peers who lose part of their own stake if the newcomer cheats. Like a lotus that cannot bloom without deep roots, an identity that costs time, money, and reputation to grow is too expensive to mass-produce, so one operator cannot cheaply spawn a thousand fake voices.
